Pianist and composer Robert Glasper has demonstrated one path that the 21st century jazz artist can follow. His melding of R&B, hip hop and jazz has proved highly successful, both critically and in the marketplace. Robert has collaborated with a diverse list of artists including Terence Blanchard, Christian McBride, Kanye West and MeShell Ndegeocello and he currently leads his own piano trio.
Robert was interviewed in Clinton, NY on February 20, 2016 by Greg Thomas, Hamilton class of ‘85.

MR: Thanks for coming early for this, I’m sure it’s going to be a great concert. This is Greg Thomas, class of ’85 and he was in the jazz program, he was in the jazz band and he’s been here for a few days. He had a great lecture the other day. And Robert Glasper, who you all know. He’s got his trio. And I’m going to turn things over to Greg and they’re going to just chat for a while and see what they come up with.
Thank you, Monk. And welcome everyone. Thank you for coming to hear this pre- concert chat. How you doing, man?
Good. I had about a five, six hour drive up here.
Yeah, from New York, yeah, from Brooklyn.

Okay. Gotcha. All right. So as you were mentioning off camera, about I guess five months ago there was an event at which I interviewed Mr. Glasper, it was an event sponsored by the National Jazz Museum in Harlem, it was a jazz and R&B discussion. So that was quite cool, and that was in front of an audience of music students at your alma mater, the New School.
